content: When rifampin is co-administered with a P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inducer, it can reduce the levels of lofepramine by increasing its metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. Lomitapide increases rifampin levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein efflux transporter, necessitating close monitoring and potential dose adjustments when used together. Rifampin decreases loperamide levels or effects via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity, requiring caution and monitoring. Similarly, rifampin reduces losartan levels by affecting hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4, necessitating careful monitoring. Rifampin also decreases lovastatin levels through P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity, requiring caution and monitoring. Rifampin affects lumacaftor/ivacaftor metabolism by inducing CYP2B6, while ivacaftor inhibits CYP2B6 substrates. This interaction requires caution and monitoring. Rifampin reduces maraviroc levels via P-glycoprotein efflux transporter activity, necessitating caution and monitoring. It also decreases marijuana levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring similar precautions. Mavorixafor increases rifampin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein, and caution is advised when co-administered with sensitive P-gp substrates due to the risk of adverse effects. Rifampin reduces medroxyprogesterone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to contraceptive failure. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Rifampin decreases mefloquine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. It also reduces melatonin levels by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism, necessitating similar precautions. It also decreases mifepristone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring similar precautions. Co-administration of rifampin with CYP3A4 inducers is not recommended for mipomersen due to the potential for increased toxicity.
